title: MRI Examinations Without Anesthesia in Children Aged 3–6 Years – Development and Validation of a Psychological Score to Reduce the Frequency of Sedation and Anesthesia
summary:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays an important role in the diagnosis of childhood illnesses. Its advantage is that it does not involve harmful radiation. The disadvantage is that the scans can take a relatively long time—up to an hour. During this time, the patient should remain as still as possible. For this reason, this procedure is often performed under anesthesia for children under 7 years of age.
For children, the procedure under anesthesia and its preparation are often anxiety-inducing. They also involve a 6-hour fast and an extended hospital stay. Furthermore, it is believed that prolonged or repeated anesthesia in young children may be associated with developmental delays, such as learning difficulties and attention deficit or hyperactivity disorders—though the evidence on this is unclear.
Our goal is to avoid general anesthesia for MRI examinations in children between the ages of 3 and 7 whenever possible. This is achieved as a standard practice through informational consultations, in which the child must be actively involved in an age-appropriate manner. This also includes a trial run in the MRI scanner and child-friendly video entertainment during the scan. 
We now wish to test the effects of the child’s developmental stage and those of intensive preparation—using coordinated games, apps, toys, and films—on the child’s willingness to tolerate the MRI scan even without anesthesia. The aim of the study is to develop a scoring system that can be used to estimate the likelihood of a successful MRI scan without anesthesia in children under the age of 7. Standardized questionnaires will also be used for this purpose. The long-term goal is to reduce the use of anesthesia in children.
conditions: Various conditions are possible; there must be a clinical indication for an MRI scan.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•Male and female patients aged 3 to 6 years and their legal guardians
•Referral with a clinical indication for an MRI (with contrast enhancement, if necessary)
•Written consent to participate in the study from the legal guardian
Exclusion criteria:
•No written consent to the study from the parents/legal guardians
